subject: Discovery recap: Tool-calling & structured output needs (JSON schema) - Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>, Samantha Lin <samantha.lin@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: Tool-calling & structured output needs (JSON schema)

Thanks for taking time today - great conversation. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we're aligned. Let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- Downstream systems fail frequently because model outputs are semi-structured free text instead of a deterministic JSON schema.
- Multiple agent workflows (order-processing, returns, fraud checks) expect strict fields; parsing errors create manual work and edge-case failures.
- Current workaround is brittle: ad-hoc regexes and post-processing in microservices.

Goals / success criteria you called out:
- Outputs must conform to a validated JSON schema with clear types (strings/enums/numbers) so downstream services can ingest reliably.
- >99% parse success for production traffic; human fallback for the rest.
- Preserve latency targets (p95 < 300ms for single-turn tool calls) and ensure cost stays within current budget envelope.

Current stack (what you told us):
- In-house orchestrator for agent routing; events wired into Kafka; services in Kubernetes.
- Model calls via a hosted provider today; looking for deterministic function/tool calling to reduce parsing complexity.
- Observability in Datadog; artifacts stored in S3.

Specific structured-output needs we discussed:
- Function/tool-calling-style responses that return a validated JSON payload (schema-driven).
- Support for multi-step agent workflows where one model response triggers subsequent tool calls (agent chaining).
- Clear error semantics and fallback policies when schema validation fails (reject vs best-effort fix vs human review).

Proposed next steps (from Redwood):
1) You share 2-3 representative prompts + a sample of current model outputs (examples + fail cases).
2) We draft a minimal JSON schema for the order-processing workflow and show a short PoC mapping (tool calling + schema enforcement).
3) 30-45 minute demo/PoC session next week to validate end-to-end deterministic output and failure handling.

Attachments: I've attached a one-pager recap and a draft schema example for the order-processing flow. (See attached: acme-discovery-recap-20260225.pdf, acme-reqs-tool-calling-schema.json)

Thanks again - looking forward to the PoC.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

+1 415-555-0124

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Tool-calling & structured output needs (JSON schema)

Thanks Marissa - this looks great and matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) For the order-processing flow we need the schema to include both a canonical order object and a separate list of actions (tool calls) with explicit identifiers so our orchestrator can route them. Example: {order: {...}, actions: [{tool: "charge-card", params: {...}}, ...]}.
2) We probably want the PoC to include the fraud-check agent chained before the charge step; if the fraud agent returns a high-risk flag, charge should not be called automatically.

Samantha and I will pull together 3 example prompts and a few current failure cases (one that caused a live outage) and drop them in the Drive link you included.

Quick scheduling - we're available Tue/Thu next week in the morning (PST). Can you propose two time slots?

Appreciate the recap - excited to see the deterministic output approach.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Automation | Acme Corp
